## Root cause

The `default/app` Deployment (rev. 2) required pod anti-affinity with `topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname`:

```yaml
affinity:
  podAntiAffinity:
    requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
    - labelSelector: {matchLabels: {app: app}}
      topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
```

The cluster has only one node (`benchmark-antiaffinity-unschedulable-2e4c26dd-control-plane`), so the new ReplicaSet pod `app-6679487758-hc2t6` could never satisfy "a separate node from every other app=app pod". The scheduler reported:

```
Warning  FailedScheduling  1 node(s) didn't match pod anti-affinity rules. preemption: 0/1 nodes are available: No preemption victims found
```

As a result the rollout was stuck at `Progressing=True` with `unavailableReplicas: 1`, while the previous ReplicaSet (`app-575b7496bc`) kept all three old pods healthy. The node itself was healthy (no taints, Ready=True), so the block was purely unschedulable by the required-hostname anti-affinity, not image or storage.

## Change made (smallest justified)

Removed only the scheduling affinity from the Deployment's pod template, leaving replicas, strategy, labels, selector and container settings untouched:

```
kubectl patch deploy app --type=json -p '[{"op":"remove","path":"/spec/template/spec/affinity"}]'  -> deployment.apps/app patched
```

## Verified outcome

- Rollout completed: `deployment "app" successfully rolled out`; `kubectl rollout status` returned success (earlier `45s timed out`).
- Replica counts match the requested count exactly: **desired 3, updated 3, ready 3, available 3**, no unavailable replicas. Deployment shows `READY 3/3`, `UP-TO-DATE 3`, `AVAILABLE 3`; the new unschedulable ReplicaSet scaled down to `0`.
- All three pods are `1/1 Running` and served traffic directly from within containers (`curl http://localhost/ → http-200` on all three).
- The stale/stuck pod `app-6679487758-hc2t6` is gone (ScaledDown / SuccessfulDelete), and the pending count is now zero.
